children: Copper falls in early Asian trade. Sentiment around base metals is likely weighed by weaker-than-expected Chinese economic data, ANZ Research analysts say in a note. "Fixed asset investment unexpectedly fell, signaling that Beijing's latest stimulus measures have yet to feed through to the world's biggest metals consumer," they add. The three-month copper futures contract on the London Metal Exchange is 0.5% lower at $13,192.50 a metric ton.(amanda.lee@wsj.com)
